items.q: In a patient with ascites presenting with acute peritonitis, which triad of ascitic fluid findings strongly points to secondary surgical peritonitis rather than spontaneous bacterial peritonitis?
opts: Protein >1 g/dL, glucose <50 mg/dL, and markedly elevated LDH (LDH ↑↑)
Protein <1 g/dL, glucose >100 mg/dL, and normal peritoneal LDH level
Protein >3 g/dL, glucose >120 mg/dL, and absence of peritoneal neutrophils
Protein <0.5 g/dL, glucose <10 mg/dL, and elevated amylase without LDH
items.exp: As noted in the book, surgical peritonitis features ascitic protein >1 g/dL, sugar (glucose) <50 mg/dL, and markedly elevated LDH (LDH ↑↑). (Book p1007)

items.q: What is the first-line empirical antibiotic regimen recommended for treating spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP), CNNA, and MNNA?
opts: Inj Cefotaxime 2 g IV TDS for 5 days
Inj Ceftriaxone 1 g IV OD for 14 days
Inj Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2 g IV BD for 10 days
Inj Vancomycin 1 g IV BD plus Metronidazole for 7 days
items.exp: The drug and regimen of choice for SBP, CNNA, and MNNA is Inj Cefotaxime 2 g IV TDS for 5 days (printed in text with degraded numeral 'ag IV TDS x 5days'). (Book p1007)

items.q: A 56-year-old cirrhotic patient recovers successfully from an acute episode of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. What secondary antibiotic prophylaxis should be instituted upon discharge?
opts: Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg OD for life
Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg BD for 7 days
Tab Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 6 months
Tab Rifaximin 550 mg BD lifelong only
items.exp: Prophylaxis with Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg OD for life is indicated for: prior SBP, Child-Pugh score ≥9, or ascitic fluid protein <1.5 g/dL in cirrhosis. (Book p1007)

items.q: In a patient with cirrhosis and ascites presenting with acute upper gastrointestinal (UGI) bleeding, the recommended prophylactic antibiotic regimen to prevent SBP is Tab Norfloxacin ________.
opts: 400 mg BD for 7 days
400 mg OD for life
200 mg OD for 14 days
800 mg stat single dose only
items.exp: For upper GI bleed in cirrhosis, the specific prophylaxis is Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg BD for 7 days. (Book p1007)

items.q: Match each clinical scenario with its recommended Norfloxacin prophylactic regimen: 1. Patient with history of prior SBP 2. Cirrhotic patient with Child's score ≥9 or ascitic protein <1.5 g/dL 3. Cirrhotic patient presenting with acute UGI bleed
opts: 1: 400 mg OD for life; 2: 400 mg OD for life; 3: 400 mg BD for 7 days
1: 400 mg BD for 7 days; 2: 400 mg BD for 7 days; 3: 400 mg OD for life
1: 400 mg OD for life; 2: 400 mg BD for 7 days; 3: 400 mg OD for life
1: 400 mg BD for 14 days; 2: 400 mg OD for life; 3: 400 mg BD for life
items.exp: Lifelong prophylaxis (Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg OD for life) is indicated for prior SBP, Child's score ≥9, and ascitic fluid protein <1.5 g/dL. Acute UGI bleed warrants short-term prophylaxis: Tab Norfloxacin 400 mg BD for 7 days. (Book p1007)

items.q: What specific clinical staging and laboratory cutoffs mandate secondary norfloxacin prophylaxis (400 mg OD lifelong) in cirrhotic ascites?
opts: Child's score ≥9 and ascitic fluid protein <1.5 g/dL
Child's score ≥10 and ascitic fluid protein <2.5 g/dL
Child's score ≥7 and ascitic fluid protein <1.0 g/dL
Child's score ≥12 and ascitic fluid protein <0.5 g/dL
items.exp: Norfloxacin 400 mg OD for life is indicated when the Child-Pugh score is ≥9 or the ascitic fluid protein is <1.5 g/dL in a cirrhotic patient. (Book p1007)
